subject: Exhibit Pricing: cap/floor application + packaging credit reconciliation
messages:
From: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@brighthealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brighthealth.com, chris.neal@brighthealth.com
Date: Mon, 26 May 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on Exhibit C – caps vs packaging credits

Marissa —

Thanks for sending the latest Exhibit C. A couple of points our procurement/legal team flagged while reviewing the pricing schedule:

1) Section 2.1 refers to a monthly 'cap' on billable tokens but Section 4 lists packaging credits to be applied to "first‑month consumption" and at renewal. It's unclear whether packaging credits reduce the cap basis (i.e., credits counted against the cap before overage), or are applied after the cap/true‑up calculation.

2) We have an internal requirement that any credits that affect the cap basis must be auditable and visible line‑by‑line on the invoice (our finance team).

3) BrightHealth would like the cap calculation to be deterministic for forecasting. Can you confirm if credits are applied pro‑rata across tiers or consumed from the lowest rate bucket first?

Please advise and, if you have a proposed reconciliation language, share it so we can circulate to our lawyers.

Best,
Emma Jenkins
Procurement Lead
BrightHealth

--
Attached: BrightHealth_Exhibit-C_v3_marked.pdf (annotated)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@brighthealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 May 2025 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit C – caps vs packaging credits

Emma —

Thanks for the careful read and the annotated copy — very helpful. High level answers while I loop in Legal for precise redline language:

- Packaging credits (the onboarding/pack credit line) are intended to reduce the amount of billable units before the cap/overage math is applied. So credits reduce the numerator used to measure consumption against the cap.
- We can provide invoice line items that show applied credits and the resulting net billable units.
- Credits are consumed against the lowest price tier first (we find that's easiest for forecasting), but I'm open to discussing deterministic pro‑rata consumption if that's a hard requirement for BrightHealth.

Karthik — would you and Ben take a quick pass at a succinct clause that we can propose back (one paragraph + example matrix)? Aim to preserve Redwood's guardrails while giving BrightHealth the visibility they need.

I have attached the proposed reconciliation matrix (draft) for your intake.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0192

Attachments: proposed-cap-reconciliation-matrix.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit C – caps vs packaging credits (legal input)

Folks —

Below is a suggested single‑paragraph amendment to Exhibit C that balances auditability with predictable economics. I've kept the drafting narrow so it won't ripple into other pricing mechanics. Please review and flag any commercial concerns.

Proposed language (for Exhibit C, insert as new Section 4.3):

"Packaging credits shall be applied to Customer consumption prior to the calculation of any monthly cap or overage. Such credits shall be reflected as distinct line items on monthly invoices showing (a) gross usage, (b) credits applied, and (c) net billable usage by pricing tier. For avoidance of doubt, credits will be consumed against the lowest price tier(s) first unless the parties agree in writing to a pro‑rata allocation. Redwood will provide a monthly reconciliation file (CSV) with token‑level aggregates sufficient for Customer finance and audit purposes.

Example: If gross usage = 1,250,000 tokens, packaging credits = 250,000 tokens, and pricing tiers are 0–500k @ $0.0008, next 500k @ $0.0006, remainder @ $0.00045, then net billable usage = 1,000,000 tokens; credits reduce the first tier fully and then the second, producing an invoice that clearly shows the applied credits, net tiers, and resulting charges."

A few notes:
- We should be comfortable committing to the CSV reconciliation file cadence (monthly) and the data fields. Operations can deliver token aggregates by day, tier, and credit category.
- If BrightHealth insists on pro‑rata consumption, that is operationally feasible but will complicate the invoice presentation and forecasting; Commercial should decide if we accept that.
- We may want to cap the audit/lookback window to 12 months to limit perpetual obligations. Adding a 12‑month audit window clause is my recommendation.

If that language looks good, Marissa can shoot it to Emma and Procurement with the draft matrix attached.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit C – caps vs packaging credits (ops note)

Quick operational confirmation from my side: we already export a daily ledger that includes gross tokens, credit adjustments (by credit type), and net tokens per model. We can extend that to include 'tier buckets' for the invoice month. The only constraint is that pro‑rata credit allocation requires a small upstream change to the billing pipeline (est. 2–3 business days dev + one QA cycle).

Given that, my recommendation: push the default "lowest tier first" language in the contract for simplicity, offer pro‑rata as a commercial option on request, and include the monthly reconciliation CSV and 12‑month audit window. That keeps commitments bounded.

—Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Emma —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the annotated PDF. Attached is a concise proposal our legal and ops teams have agreed on (see Exhibit C new Section 4.3 below). We included a short example and the draft reconciliation matrix so your finance team can validate the line‑item format.

Key takeaways:
- Packaging credits will reduce gross usage prior to cap/overage math.
- Credits consume lowest price tier first by default; pro‑rata allocation is available as an optional, billable customization.
- Redwood will deliver a monthly CSV reconciliation and retain audit data for 12 months.

Proposed Exhibit C insertion (for your review):

"Packaging credits shall be applied to Customer consumption prior to the calculation of any monthly cap or overage. Such credits shall be reflected as distinct line items on monthly invoices showing (a) gross usage, (b) credits applied, and (c) net billable usage by pricing tier. For avoidance of doubt, credits will be consumed against the lowest price tier(s) first unless the parties agree in writing to a pro‑rata allocation. Redwood will provide a monthly reconciliation file (CSV) with token‑level aggregates sufficient for Customer finance and audit purposes. The parties' right to audit consumption and credit application shall be limited to a twelve (12) month retrospective period."

Next steps: if that language is acceptable, please let me know and we can exchange a marked PDF for countersignature. If your legal team wants pro‑rata by default, tell me and I'll scope the ops impact (Ben estimates a 2–3 business day dev change).

Thanks —
Marissa
